title: Multiplication formula for Hernandez and Leclerc's quivers with potentials

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, paragraph on multiplication formula literature ("[CK08, GLS07, Pal12, XX09, KPQ23]")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The in-text citations 'Pal12' and 'XX09' are used to support the claim about the multiplication formula literature, but neither 'Pal12' nor 'XX09' appears anywhere in the reference list, which only contains BIRS09, CK08, CP95, Dim04, DWZ08, DWZ10, FM23, FR98, GLS07, GLS17, HL10, HL15, HL16, KKOP24, and KPQ23. These are unverifiable/missing citations.

The paper cites 'LM21' twice (once in the abstract, once in Remark 4.6, claiming the theorem answers 'LM21, Conjecture 5.1') but no entry for 'LM21' exists in the reference list. This is a fabricated or omitted citation that cannot be verified.

The text states "when Ext^1_A(M_1, M_2) = 1, we obtain F_{M1}·F_{M2} = F_{Y1} + F_{Y2}". Ext^1_A(M1,M2) is a vector space (or group), not a scalar, so setting it "= 1" is mathematically meaningless; the intended condition is presumably that the Ext group is one-dimensional (dim Ext^1_A(M1,M2)=1). As written, the equation is ill-posed.

Theorem 2.3 claims the Gabriel quiver of End_A(M^{-∞}), where M^{-∞} = ⊕_{a∈ℤ_{<0}} M[a,0] is built only from negatively-indexed modules, equals the full quiver Q_GLS(c) (defined on all of ℤ in (2.7)). But the paper itself earlier defines the restricted subquiver Q^-_GLS(c) as 'the inverse image of Γ^-', which is the natural candidate to match a module supported on ℤ_{<0}. Claiming equality with the full (bi-infinite) Q_GLS rather than the truncated Q^-_GLS(c) is inconsistent with the construction of M^{-∞}, and Conjecture 2.4 repeats the same mismatch by referencing 'Q_GLS' rather than Q^-_GLS.

The proof argues: 'since T appears in the right hand of the above equation, we have Y = T for all Y in the right hand of the above equation, which implies F_T = 2F_T.' This is a non-sequitur: the mere fact that T appears as one term on the right-hand side of the sum over Y does not imply that it is the *only* term, which is required to conclude F_T = 2F_T. No argument is given for why all other Y's must coincide with T.

The paper states: 'For the purposes of this paper, we assume C to be simply-laced, implying its symmetry, where C = B.' Yet later, Section 2.2 develops the generalized preprojective algebra machinery explicitly for non-simply-laced Cartan matrices (relations involving exponents -c_ij, lacing number r, general D=(d_i)), and Equation (4.2) for A_{i,r} includes correction terms for c_ji = -2 and c_ji = -3, which cannot occur for a simply-laced (ADE) Cartan matrix. This contradicts the stated blanket simply-laced assumption.

The listed affiliation is 'DEPARTMENT OF MATHEMATICS, HARBIN ENGINEERING UNIVERSITY' but the email address domain is 'mail.bnu.edu.cn', which corresponds to Beijing Normal University, not Harbin Engineering University, indicating an inconsistency in author/institutional attribution.

Theorem 4.1 states χ_q^-(W^{(i)}_{k,r-(2k-1)d_i}) = (∏_{s=1}^k Y_{i,r-(2s-1)d_i}) F_{K_{i,r}^{(i)}}, but the module defined just before (via K_{k,m}^{(i)} as kernel of a generic homomorphism I_{i,m} → I_{i,m-kb_ii}) is denoted K_{k,r}^{(i)} with both k and r as subscripts. The formula's F_{K_{i,r}^{(i)}} drops the k-index entirely, making it inconsistent with the module notation defined earlier in the same section.
